digest.headline: Crude oil prices surged above $108 a barrel as US inflation data raised rate hike bets and central bank decisions approached.

lede.b: Crude oil prices climbed above $108 a barrel after an attack near Saudi Arabia, which pushed up energy costs around the world. At the same time, new US inflation data—which measures how fast the prices of everyday goods and services are rising—caused bets on higher interest rates from the Federal Reserve to increase. A Federal Reserve rate hike means the US central bank makes borrowing money more expensive to slow down price increases. This combination of expensive oil and rising rate bets caused stock markets to drop, including the Nasdaq index falling by 1.3%.
lede.i: Crude oil prices jumped above $108 a barrel following supply fears in the Middle East, driving energy stocks higher while pressuring broader equity indices. Meanwhile, fresh US inflation readings lifted interest rate hike bets for the Federal Reserve ahead of its policy meeting. The resulting macroeconomic tightening pushed Nasdaq futures down 1.3% and caused the euro to retreat against the dollar. Traders across global exchanges also monitored currency shifts as the yen climbed and the yuan reached multi-year highs.
lede.a: Crude oil benchmarks breached $108 per barrel amid Middle East supply shocks, triggering a risk-off rotation that weighed on global equities. Concurrently, hotter US inflation prints exacerbated interest rate hike expectations for the Federal Reserve, compressing tech valuations and driving Nasdaq futures down 1.3%. The resulting dollar dynamics and currency appreciation forced speculative carry trade unwinds, notably pushing the yen to multi-month highs and compelling the People's Bank of China to anchor its daily reference rate at 6.7698.

stories.t: OPEC Production Dynamics and Global Oil Impacts
stories.b: Global oil prices rose quickly after an attack linked to Saudi Arabia. Higher crude prices pushed stock indexes like the FTSE 100 higher in early trading. At the same time, Nigeria reached an oil output of 1.68mbpd in August. This production level met its official OPEC quota target for the fourth month in a row. OPEC is a group of countries that manage oil supplies together.
stories.i: Global crude prices surged following an attack near Saudi Arabia, driving equity benchmarks higher. Nigeria maintained its compliance with OPEC production caps by pumping 1.678mbpd through August. This output level marked the fourth consecutive month Nigeria met its assigned cartel ceiling. Cartel quota discipline directly influences global supply balances and benchmark pricing.
stories.a: Geopolitical risk premium re-priced rapidly across crude benchmarks following a reported attack on Saudi assets. Concurrently, NUPRC data confirmed Nigerian August output at 1.68mbpd, sustaining compliance with OPEC parameters for a fourth straight month. This adherence by key producers limits supply elasticity while inventories face ongoing drawdowns. The interaction between Middle Eastern security incidents and card quota adherence dictates prompt-month futures volatility.

politics.b: Saudi Arabia manages its national oil resources through state firms. It coordinates oil production rules with other nations in the OPEC alliance. These international rules control how much fuel reaches global markets.
politics.i: Saudi energy policy relies on state-controlled production capacity and international cartel coordination. The Kingdom utilizes organizations like OPEC to manage global supply quotas. Geopolitical stability directly affects state-led joint ventures and regional export infrastructure.
politics.a: Saudi resource sovereignty relies on state-directed capital allocation through Aramco and strategic multilateral coordination via OPEC. The state leverages its spare capacity to anchor geopolitical influence across international refining joint ventures. Domestic security and infrastructure protection remain prerequisites for maintaining projected capital expenditures.
